How it works

The game should be the hard part.

  1. 01

    Bring your worlds.

    Pick a DRM-free folder or ZIP. Nexus keeps a validated private copy — your originals are never touched.

  2. 02

    Let Nexus handle the details.

    It reads your chipset and GPU, then prepares the runtime. Community profile matching is planned.

  3. 03

    Make yourself at home.

    Turn sideways and play. Touch overlays and controller input are part of the vision.

Why Nexus

Less tinkering. More playing.

Running PC games on Android today usually means a weekend of guides. This is the part we want to remove.

the-usual-way.sh
  1. $ create a Wine prefix
  2. $ export BOX64_DYNAREC_* flags
  3. $ hunt for a Turnip driver build
  4. $ pick a DXVK version
  5. $ edit the registry by hand
  6. $ map every control yourself
  7. ! crash · retry · repeat

The stack

From tap to game, layer by layer.

Every layer is open source and pinned, so results are repeatable on the same device.

  1. 01 · Interface

    Flutter shell

    Home, Library, Device and Settings in Dart.

  2. 02 · Bridge

    Kotlin host

    Typed Pigeon APIs, imports and the SQLite library.

  3. 03 · Native

    C++ core

    Vulkan device profiling and the packaged launcher.

  4. 04 · Runtime

    Wine + Box64

    x86-64 Windows code on ARM64, 4 KB and 16 KB pages.

  5. 05 · Play

    Your game

    Running from your own private library.

Under the hood

Small screen. Full ambition.

Thoughtful engineering behind a simpler experience — honestly labeled by what ships today and what’s next.

Available

Local game library

Folder and ZIP imports into app-private copies, with paged search, title edits and SHA-256 details.

Available

Bounded, safe imports

Path-traversal, link, ZIP64 and compression-bomb checks, with progress, cancellation and recovery.

Available

Knows your device

A typed native bridge reports Android API, SoC, ABIs, RAM and the Vulkan renderer.

Experimental

A real Windows runtime

Pinned Wine 10.10 and Box64 launch x86-64 executables on 4 KB and 16 KB ARM64 hosts. Emulator-tested, opt-in.

Planned

Built to adapt

Cloud profile matching that recognizes evolving Snapdragon chipsets.

Planned

Your way to play

Touch overlays, controller input and Turnip / DXVK graphics for Direct3D games.

FAQs

A few things you might be wondering.

Ask on GitHub
Can I download Nexus-PC yet?

The project is in its development stage. There isn’t a public game-running release yet. Follow the GitHub repository for progress and future releases.

Will it work on my phone?

The focus is ARM64 Android 12+ phones with Snapdragon chips and Adreno graphics. So far only the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 has passed the Phase 0 proof; other chips in the list above are targets, not guarantees.

Does it run on iPhone or iPad?

No. Nexus-PC is an Android app. Apple A-series and M-series chips run iOS and iPadOS, which this project doesn’t target.

Will every PC game work?

Compatibility is still being evaluated. Only Windows GDI titles have been tested so far; Direct3D, sound and controllers are unverified. Results will depend on your hardware and the translation stack.

Are games streamed from the cloud?

No. The goal is to run imported games on your Android device using translation runtimes. The planned cloud service matches device and game profiles; it doesn’t stream gameplay.

Do my original game files get modified?

Never. Imports create a validated, app-private copy. Your source folder or ZIP is left exactly as it was.

How can I help build it?

Explore the repository, share ideas through GitHub issues, or contribute code. Device testing and compatibility reports will be valuable as the engine matures.
